title: Turning down Ellington's Sacred Concert work and the nudist camp joke
summary: Newly settled in Los Angeles, Jones declined to return east for the second Sacred Concert, with a story about Duke's Reno suite.

venues.name: Cathedral of St. John the Divine

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: You were up in Reno writing with Duke on something. What project was that?
He wanted me to go back to do the
Sacred Concert with Alice Babbs.
Which one, one or two? That would have been two, number two, in 1968.
Yeah. In the --
St. John's.

Yeah. And I had just moved out this way at that point, and my wife and I had gotten settled, had a nice apartment and everything, and to get established as a resident musician you can't keep going in and out of town.
Right.

You know, you get off the calling lists. You know, people don't call you because they don't know where you are or whether you're going to be able to make it or not. And I just didn't -- I didn't go. That was the hardest thing for me to do, and it was so amazing, because that night, it was 12:00 o'clock. There was one plane coming back here and another plane going to New York, around 12:00 o'clock, or maybe 10 or 15 minutes apart. And it took me a long time to make up my mind on it. And I stayed there a few days, and -- because he -- he -- he paid me. I didn't do one bit of work and he paid me. He had a big suite there with nothing but pretty ladies in there.
Well, he usually worked that way.
Yeah. And then I just told him, 'Edward, I cannot work in a nudist camp.'
(Laughter)
"You can't get a note out of me like this."
(Laughter)

He laughed about that quite often. He said, "Many, how you doing with your nudist camps?" No, I can't get any work done this way. But as I was saying, I was just getting established here and -- which I think was a wise move. I came back home.
Uh-huh.
You know, because had I gone to New York I'd have been still on the road.
Yes. Yes.

You know? And no, I just -- because at that point in my life, I mean everything -- I wanted to get settled and live a little different life, because I'd had enough of all those cold winters back there at that point. I would like to go back for a visit, because I have a whole lot of friends there, but I don't think I could just live like I once did, when I was much younger and could take it, you know?
Uh-huh.
And try to keep up with New York, you know. But now it's time for me to kind of simmer down some.
